items.text: "Career Assessment" Has Become "Career "Career Assessment" Has Become "Career assessment" has become an umbrella term. Under that umbrella sit at least four different kinds of tools, and they answer different questions.

items.heading: A Platform That Calls
items.text: A Platform That Calls A platform that calls a personality quiz or interest inventory an "aptitude test" without measuring reasoning ability is stretching the term, not testing aptitude.

items.heading: Many Providers Charge a Substantial
items.text: Many providers charge a substantial one-time fee for a formal aptitude battery, often positioned as the "real" or "scientific" option versus anything free. That framing deserves a closer look rather than automatic trust.

items.heading: The Classic Reference Point
items.text: The classic reference point for a real aptitude test is something like DBDA or CII: named reasoning categories (numerical, verbal, logical, spatial) with an actual score per category, not a single vague label.

items.heading: Free Does Not Automatically Mean
items.text: Free does not automatically mean weak on the aptitude dimension, and a price tag does not automatically mean the reasoning categories are more current or rigorous.

items.heading: The Free Assessments Here Include
items.text: The free assessments here include reasoning and ability signals as part of a broader, updated, AI-powered read, genuinely useful for narrowing a decision, though it is not a standalone, formally standardised psychometric battery in the classic DBDA/CII mould.
